analysis:
Examined all supplied source, patches and metadata against the canonical definition index and selected T-041 detail. StartupPreload.swift:307-310 now queues memory-skipped, memory-failed and unattempted candidates for recovery, excluding cancelled, shutting-down and explicitly stopped runs. Existing startup loads retain no-eviction admission (359), and self-test retirement retains hash-bound refusal and unadvertising (405-459). Serve.swift:565 includes the active recovery task in shutdown cancellation/waiting.

Both shutdown paths now use StartupShutdown.swift:77-97's bounded per-slot teardown rather than waiting indefinitely. It retains unfinished slots, launches unload tasks, and can return with native retirement unresolved; Serve.swift:586-591 still separately requires native MiMo owners to drain. This improves stop availability but makes process-exit and retained-owner behavior important to A-001/A-018, TB-007, T-028 and T-059. No supported regression is established: supplied callers do not demonstrate resumed serving or unsafe reclamation after bounded teardown.

Integration must examine ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery's selection filtering, retry pacing, memory/slot admission, failed-self-test refusal and add-on-hold fence (TB-012/T-059), including enqueueing while servingDrain refuses. Also verify that shutdown callers exit rather than reuse the loop after abandoned slots, and that unload/native retirement ownership remains safe when pre-registration shutdown clears the MLX cache (StartupShutdown.swift patch head:63). These are unverified contracts, not observed missing controls. The supplied changes do not directly modify encryption, cache scope/TTL, registration capabilities, attestation binding, credentials or billing. Unchanged callers and native unload implementations were not supplied.
